# v0.2.0 — Registry Cleaner, Applications page and the new sidebar UI

## Registry Cleaner (Windows)

A full registry cleaner in the style of CCleaner's Registry tool, with all 15
cleaning rules: Missing Shared DLLs, Unused File Extensions, ActiveX and
Class Issues, Type Libraries, Applications, Fonts, Application Paths, Help
Files, Installer remnants, Obsolete Software, Run At Startup, Start Menu
Ordering, MUI Cache, Sound Events and Windows Services.

- Isolated on its own page with a **checkbox per rule** (selection persisted
  between sessions), so you decide exactly what gets scanned and fixed
- Every rule only flags entries that point to files that no longer exist —
  the same objective criteria CCleaner uses; umbrella keys such as
  `Microsoft` are never touched
- Fixes are confirmed in a dialog and recorded in the activity log
- The rule engine is fully unit-tested without Windows (registry reads are
  abstracted behind a trait with a mock)

## Applications page (beta)

The Applications tab now lists installed programs, **least-used first**,
with disk size, last-used date and one-click uninstall:

- Linux: desktop files mapped to pacman/dpkg/rpm packages, plus flatpak and
  snap installs; uninstall goes through `pkexec` (polkit password prompt) —
  the app never handles passwords
- Windows: registry uninstall entries with UserAssist last-run times
- macOS: `/Applications` bundles, with last-used from Spotlight metadata

## New navigation

- Sidebar with one page per feature (Overview, Registry, Browsers, Trash,
  Messenger Media, Applications, Settings) following the new mockup
- Redesigned Overview, per-page layouts with proper spacing, and a
  CPU/MEMORY/DISK monitor bar
- The results page is a regular page now — navigating away no longer leaves
  it floating on top, and the back button returns to where you opened it from
- App version shown in the sidebar

## Performance

Scans run on all cores now, with benchmarks to show for it (release build,
warm cache):

| scan | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| duplicates | 7.3s | 1.2s |
| orphan | 2.7s | 0.5s |
| large & old | 1.4s | 0.25s |

- Parallel directory walk with a std-only worker pool (no new dependencies)
- Scan progress is throttled (80ms) — no more IPC/DOM storm per folder
- Metadata from the walk is reused end-to-end; files are never stat-ted twice
- Duplicate candidates are pre-filtered with a 64 KiB head hash before any
  full-file read, and hashing/confirmation run in parallel

## Fixes

- Browser scan now covers **Brave, Edge, Chromium, flatpak and snap** cache
  roots on every platform (previously Chromium-based browsers other than
  Chrome were silently skipped)
- A UI bug where every category was reported as "failed" after a scan
- The updater pipeline now ships signed update artifacts and a complete
  `latest.json` for all platforms
